questions.question: When you start a vehicle, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: When an engine starts, the coolant temperature should gradually increase toward the normal operating temperature.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Not helpful, because you cannot do anything about problems far away.

questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to notice hazards and respond safely.

questions.question: You should hold the steering wheel with:

options.text: One hand to keep the other free.
One hand at a time, switching hands.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides.

questions.question: Parking brakes should be:

options.text: Tested only after driving some distance.

questions.explanation: Always check your parking brakes before driving. This is part of checking your vehicle. If the parking brakes do not hold, your vehicle needs to be fixed.

questions.question: When visibility is poor and other vehicles are nearby, you should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving near other vehicles in poor visibility, such as at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. High beams can make it hard for other drivers to see.

questions.question: To parallel park, you should:

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on your right. Then back into the space while keeping the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: Black ice is:

options.text: Ice that is black from dirt on the road.

questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. The road looks wet. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet and the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: Texting while driving compared to talking on a phone while driving is:
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on the phone. It distracts you mentally and physically.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should not be more than:
questions.explanation: Steering wheel play of more than 10 degrees makes steering difficult.

questions.question: To help prevent drowsiness while driving, you should:

options.text: Get enough sleep the night before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get enough sleep the night before your trip.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Get a full night's sleep before driving. Other helpful steps include having someone ride with you, scheduling trips when you are normally awake, and avoiding medicines that cause drowsiness. Regular exercise also helps you feel more alert while driving.

questions.question: Your wheel bearings and seals should be:
questions.explanation: Check that wheel bearings and seals are not leaking during an inspection.

questions.question: If you feel sleepy while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving and finish your trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel sleepy while driving, stop and get sleep. This is the only safe choice. Fighting drowsiness is dangerous and causes many deadly crashes. Energy pills may keep you awake but will not help you think clearly. When the pill wears off, you will be even more tired than before.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Avoid using mirrors in heavy traffic.
Look only at the front and right side of your vehicle.
Look at the front, sides, and rear of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the front, sides, and rear of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must know what is happening around your vehicle at all times. Check ahead and use your mirrors regularly on both sides while driving.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle must:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher unless carrying hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher unless traveling through remote areas.
Always have at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always have at least one fire extinguisher.
questions.explanation: All vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. When inspecting a commercial vehicle, check for at least one fire extinguisher, spare fuses (or circuit breakers), and warning devices for when the vehicle is parked.

questions.question: A ramp's posted speed limit:

options.text: Works for some vehicles but may be too fast for a large commercial truck.
Is just a suggestion and can be exceeded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Works for some vehicles but may be too fast for a large commercial truck.
questions.explanation: Exit and entrance ramps show speeds safe for cars. But these speeds may be too fast for large or heavily loaded trucks. Commercial drivers often need to drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: Carry-on baggage must be:
questions.explanation: Passengers should not leave baggage in doorways or aisles. Baggage must be secured to prevent damage, allow the driver to move freely, let people exit safely in an emergency, and protect riders from injury if items shift.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, it should be:
questions.explanation: Check that no parts of the exhaust system are loose, broken, or missing.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of bad brake drums or shoes?

options.text: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid
questions.explanation: Bad brake problems include cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin.

questions.question: How can you avoid drowsiness on a trip?

options.text: Get three hours of sleep beforehand.

questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue while driving, get seven to eight hours of sleep beforehand, drive during your normal waking hours, plan breaks during your trip, and exercise regularly.

questions.question: Parked delivery trucks are hazardous because:

options.text: People hurrying to exit may not check for other vehicles.
Packages often fall into the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: People hurrying to exit may not check for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery trucks are dangerous because the driver may pull into traffic suddenly without warning, or step out without checking for other vehicles.
